name: react-doctor
description: Your agent writes bad React. This catches it
readmeExcerpt: Your agent writes bad React, this catches it. React Doctor deterministically scans your codebase and finds issues across state and effects, performance, architecture, security, accessibility, and maintainability. It highlights overly complex React functions and repeated JSX trees that are good candidates for composition. Works across React frameworks and React-enabled sites - Next.js, Vite, Astro, TanStack, React Native, Expo, you name it. [Website →](https://react.doctor/docs) ## Install ### 1. Quick start Run this at your project root to get an audit. ```bash npx react-doctor@latest ``` https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/07cc88d9-9589-44c3-aa73-5d603cb1c570 ### 2. Install for agents Once you have an audit, you can install the skill for your coding agent to learn from the issues and fix them in the future. ```bash npx react-doctor@latest install ``` Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, and many more. ### 3. Run in CI React Doctor reviews every pull request and reports only the issues your change introduced, not your existing backlog. Set it up with one command: ```bash npx react-doctor@latest ci install ``` This adds the workflow, scans every pull request, and posts a summary comment. Change the gate, scan scope, and comments anytime with `react-doctor ci config`, and bump the action with `react-doctor ci upgrade`. GitHub Actions is fully supported; GitLab CI gets a gate-only scaffold. [CI docs →](https://react.doctor/ci) ### 4. Configure rules You can configure which rules to run and how to run them in `doctor.config.ts`. [Learn more →](https://react.doctor/docs/configuration/config-files) ## Telemetry The CLI reports crashes, basic run traces, and anonymous usage counters to [Sentry](https://sentry.io/) to help us fix bugs and prioritize work. We collect: - Environment: CLI version, platform, Node version - Invocation: which command, package manager, and run context (whether it's local vs. CI vs. coding agent) - Project shape: framework, React version, TypeScript, project size (NO file contents) - Rules fired: rule names and counts only (e.g. `react-doctor/no-array-index-as-key`) (NO code or specific findings) - De-minified React Doctor CLI stack traces To opt out, run: `npx react-doctor@latest --no-telemetry` ## Contributing [Issues welcome!](https://github.com/millionco/react-doctor/issues) MIT-licensed

aiSummary.oneLiner: A deterministic CLI code reviewer that identifies performance and architectural issues in React and Next.js applications.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: React Doctor operates as an automated, specialized code reviewer that strictly analyzes React-based codebases. It deterministically flags performance bottlenecks like unnecessary re-renders, improper hook dependencies, and bloated components across frameworks like Next.js and Vite. The tool provides a CLI for local audits, a GitHub Action for scanning pull requests dynamically, and an installable skill for AI coding agents. It surfaces actionable health reports with exact code snippets to help engineers quickly remediate architectural debt. The tool leverages deep AST analysis to aggressively root out performance bottlenecks like unnecessary re-renders. It functions proactively within the CI/CD pipeline, catching architectural flaws before they are merged into production.
keyFeatures: Deterministic scanning: Reliably uncovers structural and performance issues in React applications without false positives.
Hook dependency checking: Automatically flags missing or incorrect dependency arrays in useEffect and useMemo implementations.
Dynamic PR auditing: Integrates into CI pipelines to report only new regressions introduced by a specific pull request.
Agent skill capability: Installs into AI assistants like Cursor or Claude Code to guide them toward writing optimized React.
Broad framework support: Works seamlessly across Next.js, Vite, Astro, React Native, and Expo environments.
AST Deep Analysis: Parses component trees to identify structural flaws beyond simple regex matching
Proactive Tech Debt Prevention: Integrates into workflows to block poorly structured code from merging
